title: Physics — arXiv announcement batch, 19 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. The ordering is inferred from concrete results, cross-listing and checkable metadata; the papers are newly announced and citation/attention evidence is sparse, so this is not a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
sections.abstract: The authors report that optimized syndrome extraction on an IBM Nighthawk r2 reduces surface-code memory error rates, with distance-3-to-6 suppression factors of 1.68 in Z memory and 1.85 in X memory.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report median per-round logical error reductions by factors of 3.8 (X) and 1.4 (Z) with circuit optimizations; increasing protected distance from 3 to 6 yields suppression factors 1.68 (Z) and 1.85 (X).
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; rotated surface-code memory on an IBM Nighthawk r2 processor, up to 150 syndrome rounds, maximum-likelihood decoding.
sections.unique_caveat: The distance advantage weakens in long memory runs; long-lived correlations may indicate a persistent error component, and results vary by processor placement.

sections.title: Reactor Antineutrino Detection with JUNO-TAO: Commissioning Performance and First Results
sections.abstract: The JUNO-TAO collaboration reports commissioning performance and first reactor-on/off data from a 2.8-ton cryogenic antineutrino detector 43.2 m from a reactor core.
sections.claimed_result: The collaboration reports about 2.8% energy resolution for a central Ge-68 calibration source, about 90% of channels retained after quality selection, and an excess of inverse-beta-decay candidates in reactor-on data relative to reactor-off data.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; TAO commissioning and 31.3 days reactor-on plus 29.4 days reactor-off data.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a detector-performance and initial-rate report, not the final high-precision reactor antineutrino spectrum measurement; energy resolution varies by calibration source and position.

sections.title: Observation of the Ξ_b⁻ → Ξ⁻μ⁺μ⁻ and study of the Ξ_b⁻ → Ξ⁻ψ(2S) decays
sections.abstract: LHCb reports the first observation of the rare Ξ_b⁻ → Ξ⁻μ⁺μ⁻ decay and measures its branching fraction in dimuon-mass intervals, alongside a ratio for the ψ(2S) and J/ψ channels.
sections.claimed_result: The collaboration measures the integrated branching fraction as (118 ± 24 ± 7 ± 38) × 10⁻⁸ and the ψ(2S)-to-J/ψ branching-fraction ratio as 0.491 ± 0.041 ± 0.019.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; LHCb proton-proton collision data at 7, 8, and 13 TeV, corresponding to 1, 2, and 6 fb⁻¹.
sections.unique_caveat: The largest quoted uncertainty on the integrated branching fraction comes from the normalization branching fraction, whose uncertainty is dominated by SU(3)-breaking effects.

sections.title: Complete g⁶ pressure of hot Yang-Mills theory
sections.abstract: The authors calculate the full order-g⁶ pressure of hot SU(3) Yang-Mills theory, combining newly evaluated four-loop contributions with known electric- and magnetic-scale terms.
sections.claimed_result: The authors evaluate nine previously unknown nonfactorizing four-loop sum-integrals, complete the hard-scale contribution for general SU(Nc), and obtain the complete O(g⁶) pressure for SU(3) after combining known contributions.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical/computational; thermal loop-tree duality calculations with local UV/IR subtractions, combined with existing scale contributions and compared with lattice-simulation data.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a weak-coupling theoretical calculation, not a direct measurement; the SU(3) result combines contributions from different momentum scales, and its usefulness depends on the temperature regime where the expansion is controlled.

sections.title: The pressure of the gluon plasma at O(g_s⁶), perturbatively
sections.abstract: The authors compute a four-loop hard-scale matching correction and say it completes the high-temperature gluon-plasma pressure through O(g_s⁶), in agreement within uncertainties with an earlier lattice-data fit.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a four-loop hard-scale matching correction whose value agrees, within uncertainties, with the value previously obtained by fitting the perturbative series to continuum-extrapolated lattice data.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical/computational; perturbative high-temperature calculation compared with a lattice-data fit.
sections.unique_caveat: The comparison is with an earlier fit to lattice data rather than a new experiment; the result remains a perturbative, high-temperature statement.

sections.title: Ionic switching between supermagnetic states
sections.abstract: The authors report reversible room-temperature Li-ion-driven switching between superferromagnetic and superspin-glass states in partially lithiated NiO, persisting over subsequent lithiation/delithiation cycles.
sections.claimed_result: The authors attribute the superferromagnetic state to a fragmented nanoscale-Ni network formed by lithiation, and the superspin-glass state to partial NiO regeneration during delithiation.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; room-temperature lithiation/delithiation of NiO with magnetic characterization.
sections.unique_caveat: The result and proposed mechanism are specific to this NiO-based system; the abstract does not establish generality across materials.

sections.title: Gravitational Waves as a Probe of Multi-Fluid Cosmologies: General Formalism and the Case of Cosmological Stasis
sections.abstract: The authors extend scalar-induced gravitational-wave calculations to multi-fluid early-universe cosmologies and show how fluid composition can alter the predicted spectrum and present-day abundance.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that a multi-fluid composition can change scalar-induced gravitational-wave signals beyond what is captured by the overall expansion rate, and that stasis can yield spectra and present-day abundances differing from radiation domination.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; formal analysis and model predictions, not a reported gravitational-wave detection.
sections.unique_caveat: Predicted signals depend on the assumed early-universe history and multi-fluid model; the paper does not report observational confirmation.

sections.title: Near-Extremal Black-Hole Formation Observed from Null Infinity
sections.abstract: Numerical evolutions of a spherically symmetric Einstein-Maxwell-charged-scalar system form near-extremal black holes, with their charge-to-mass ratios inferred from observables at future null infinity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report formation up to charge-to-mass ratio 0.993 from regular, horizon-free, superextremal initial data in their fully nonlinear evolutions.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; fully nonlinear numerical evolution of the spherically symmetric Einstein-Maxwell-charged-scalar system.
sections.unique_caveat: “Observed” refers to extracting signals at future null infinity in the simulations, not an astronomical observation; the setup is spherically symmetric and uses a charged scalar field.

sections.title: Eulerian ion energisation in three-dimensional hybrid-Vlasov-Maxwell turbulence
sections.abstract: Three-dimensional hybrid-Vlasov-Maxwell simulations show that the contribution of agyrotropic ion currents to energisation varies strongly between the two studied ion-plasma beta values.
sections.claimed_result: The agyrotropic term accounts for 21% of energisation at βᵢ₀ = 0.25 and 91% at βᵢ₀ = 4; the dominant instantaneous term changes with βᵢ₀.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; decaying turbulence in three-dimensional hybrid Vlasov-Maxwell simulations at βᵢ₀ = 0.25 and 4.
sections.unique_caveat: Conclusions are based on the two simulated initial beta regimes and resolved scales; they do not by themselves establish the same partition in every astrophysical or laboratory plasma.
